result.topic_en: Euler assigns lengths, cross-sections and inclinations to the successive parts of a pipe system, defines the effluent velocity height v and the pressures at each section, and gives the chain of formulas linking these pressures when friction acts.

Ponatur enim pro ſingulis partibus
$AF = a$; amplitudo $AA = ff$; et ang. cum verticali $= \epsilon$
$BC = b$; amplitudo $BB = gg$; et ang. cum verticali $= \zeta$
$CD = c$; amplitudo $CC = hh$; et ang. cum verticali $= \eta$
$DE = d$; amplitudo $DD = ii$; et ang. cum verticali $= \theta$
Denique ſit orificium $EE = kk$, quod hactenus per $hh$ indicauimus.
35. Sit denique $v$ altitudo debita celeritati, qua aqua per orificium $EE = kk$ effluet, ac ponatur ſtatus compreſſionis aquae
in $AA = l$ quae eſt altitudo circiter 30 pedum
in $BB = P$
in $CC = Q$
in $DD = R$
in $EE = l$, cum hic fiat effluxus.
36. Quodſi iam ratiocinium vt ante inſtituamus, reperiemus:
$P = l e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{f}} + \frac{f}{\alpha}\left(1 - e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{f}}\right) + k^4 v\left(\frac{1}{f^4} - \frac{1}{g^4}\right)$
$Q = P e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}} + \frac{g}{\alpha}\left(1 - e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}\right)\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta + k^4 v\left(\frac{1}{g^4} - \frac{1}{h^4}\right)$
$R = Q e^{\frac{-\alpha c}{h}} + \frac{h}{\alpha}\left(1 - e^{\frac{-\alpha c}{h}}\right)\mathrm{cof.}\,\eta + k^4 v\left(\frac{1}{h^4} - \frac{1}{i^4}\right)$
$= R e^{\frac{-\alpha d}{i}} + \frac{i}{\alpha}\left(1 - e^{\frac{-\alpha d}{i}}\right)\mathrm{cof.}\,\theta + k^4 v\left(\frac{1}{i^4} - \frac{1}{k^4}\right)$
